basis.quote: I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area.
basis.interpretation: Current allergic contact dermatitis with pruritic vesicular lesions on bilateral forearms, progressing locally since Saturday exposure.
Denies systemic symptoms and respiratory involvement, reducing concern for severe allergic reaction or anaphylaxis.

output.reason: Contact dermatitis with active spread warrants clinician review for topical or systemic anti-inflammatory therapy and itch management, but no emergency features are reported.

Localized itchy blistery rash confined to both forearms after a reported poison ivy exposure, with no reported fever or breathing trouble, is manageable with over-the-counter care and a clear worsening safety net.
output.patientMessage: You can start self-care at home now: wash skin and clothing, use cool compresses, and ask your pharmacist about an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and an anti-itch antihistamine. This pattern fits a poison ivy contact rash. Message us for clinician review if the rash becomes painful, warm and tender rather than itchy, spreads to your face or genitals, or isn't improving over the next week.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy)
Secondary bacterial skin infection if the area becomes painful/tender

redFlags.concern: Rash spread beyond forearms (face/genitals) or extensive body area
Pain, warmth or tenderness suggesting cellulitis

output.vitalSigns: No vital-sign values reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
